'''Christopher D. Evans''' (born 1951 in [[Tredegar]], Wales)<ref name="entry">{{cite news | url=http://www.literaturewales.org/writers-of-wales/i/129644/desc/evans-christopher/| title=Evans, Christopher D.| work=[[Literature Wales]]| accessdate=2014-09-19| url-status=dead| archiveurl=https://archive.today/20140919053107/http://www.literaturewales.org/writers-of-wales/i/129644/desc/evans-christopher/| archivedate=2014-09-19}}</ref> is a British [[science fiction]] writer and children's author.  His novels include ''Capella's Golden Eyes'' (1980); ''[[The Insider (Evans novel)|The Insider]]'' (1981); ''Mortal Remains'' (1995); and ''Ice Tower'' (2000).  He is the co-editor (with [[Robert Holdstock]]) of three original SF anthologies, ''[[Other Edens]]'' (1987); ''Other Edens II'' (1988); and ''Other Edens III'' (1989).

Evans won the [[BSFA award]] for the 1993 novel ''[[Aztec Century]]'', which [[Iain M. Banks]] described as '...intelligent, finely written, and towards the end, absolutely nail-biting.'{{Citation needed|date=August 2020}}

In addition to his works for younger readers, he wrote the tie-in novelisation of the film ''[[Innerspace]]'' (1987). Evans published these books using a pseudonym.  His book ''Omega'', an [[alternate history]] thriller, was released by [[PS Publishing]] in 2008.  It was his first novel for adults in a decade.

== Selected works ==

=== Series novels ===
{{anchor|The Hood's Army Trilogy}}

;Hood's Army (as Nathan Elliott)
The ''Hood's Army'' trilogy is a series of young adult science fiction novels by Evans, but written under the pseudonym of "Nathan Elliott."  The trilogy was published in 1986.<ref>{{Cite web | date=2014-09-19 |title=Evans, Christopher | url=http://www.literaturewales.org/writers-of-wales/i/129644/desc/evans-christopher/ | archive-url=https://archive.today/20140919053107/http://www.literaturewales.org/writers-of-wales/i/129644/desc/evans-christopher/ | url-status=dead | archive-date=2014-09-19 |access-date=2020-07-12 |website=Literature Wales}}</ref>  The books that make up the series are entitled ''Earth Invaded''; ''Slaveworld''; and ''The Liberators''.  They tell of a near future in which Earth is conquered by an alien race named the K'Thraa, and of the resistance force which battles them.
